data.narrative:
Electric Hydrogen, a Series C climate and energy company founded by Raffi Garabedian and David Eaglesham, commands a current post-money valuation of $1.0B following $700M in total capital raised. The valuation assessment employs a peer universe of three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables: Redwood Materials (Series D, $6.0B), KoBold Metals (Series C, $3.0B), and Amogy (Series C, $700M), anchored within a broader 9-company private and public comp set in Climate & Energy.

Two triangulation methods prove applicable. Stage-progression analysis applies a standard 1.7x Series C step-up multiplier to the $1.0B last post-money valuation, implying $1.7B. Peer-median valuation across the three comparables yields $3.0B, reflecting the wide dispersion in the peer set ($700M to $6.0B). The median peer—KoBold Metals at $3.0B—sits substantially above Electric Hydrogen's current mark, though Amogy's $700M valuation demonstrates material heterogeneity in stage-equivalent pricing within the sector.

The triangulated analysis supports a range of $1.4B (low) to $3.4B (high), with a median estimate of $2.3B. This implies meaningful upside from the current $1.0B valuation. Key uncertainties include the wide peer valuation dispersion (5.7x range) and the nascent stage of comparable companies, limiting confidence in normalized multiples. The stage-progression and peer-median methods diverge by $1.3B, reflecting sector-specific maturity and capital intensity dynamics.
